live_web_research.page_text: [2610.12369] Embodied Turing Machines: Stateful Code for Robot Recursive Self-Improvement Skip to main content Search arXiv Press Enter to search · Advanced search --> Computer Science > Robotics arXiv:2610.12369 (cs) [Submitted on 8 Oct 2026] Title: Embodied Turing Machines: Stateful Code for Robot Recursive Self-Improvement Authors: Kairui Hu , Siyuan Hu , Fangzhou Hong , Zhaoxi Chen , Ziwei Liu View a PDF of the paper titled Embodied Turing Machines: Stateful Code for Robot Recursive Self-Improvement, by Kairui Hu and 4 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Most robot policies keep a model in the control loop: a VLA maps observations to actions, and an Agent Harness, such as Agent-as-Policy or Harness VLA queries a VLM for decision making at run time. We propose a different view: the embodied world is an Embodied Turing Machine, whose tape is the robot and environment state and rules are the policy. If this state can be represented accurately, the decision making can be written entirely in code. We therefore propose Code-Only-as-Policy (COAP): code measures and tracks the robot, environment, and task state from camera images and proprioception, and makes every decision from it. The same code applies across episodes, and different tasks share one library without a VLM or VLA in the loop. Compared with VLAs and Agent Harnesses, we analyze three advantages of COAP: (i) Explicit State: the state can be stored in code; (ii) Execution: code makes decision making controllable, recovers from failures flexibly, and runs fast and cheaply online; (iii) Extensibility: new tasks reuse, inherit, or extend the shared library, so capabilities can accumulate over tasks. These advantages make COAP a suitable medium for recursive self-improvement (RSI): coding agents develop the library in a closed loop, and each change is explicit and controllable. On RoboDojo's 42 bimanual tasks, the resulting library reaches a success rate of 70.24% without a model at test time. The upper bound of COAP lies in how accurately the state is represented for decision making and how robust the code logic is. We thus propose COAP as a new paradigm for embodied tasks; since it applies across episodes, it can also serve as an efficient data engine for VLAs and Agent Harnesses. live_web_research.page_text: Embodied Turing Machines 1:27 · sound on We formulate embodied tasks as SWE problems and explore how far Code-Only-as-Policy can go, analyzing its strengths and limitations. Benchmark results serve to validate the approach, not as the objective. We also view COAP as a complement to model-based methods, as it generates large-scale, controllable trajectories. Embodied Turing Machine & The Exploration of Code-Only-As-Policy (COAP) How far can code-only policies go? We view the embodied world as an Embodied Turing Machine, whose tape is the robot and environment state and rules are the policy. What if a robot policy didn't need a VLM or VLA in its runtime control loop? We want to explore the limit of a different paradigm: Can code-only-as-policy go surprisingly far in embodied intelligence? Where does it work, and where does it break? Data engine. Given offline time, coding agents iterate on a reusable code library. A working program then generates diverse trajectories efficiently and at scale for policy training. Stable, fast execution. Decisions are explicit code, and no model is queried at run time, so execution is stable, fast and cheap. This suits industrial settings where the state can be measured reliably. Generalization trade-off. Zero-shot generalization is difficult for code and generally calls for an agent in the loop. Code, however, is reusable: with offline development, it extends to new tasks and scenes. One shared library. Cross-episode, cross-task. Fast No model at runtime. Stable Decisions are code, not samples. Every decision is explicit. Cross-episode One program for every episode. Fixes carry over. Reusable Shared library. Easy to extend, reuse and inherit. Data engine Efficient trajectory generation for VLA, Agent-as-Policy and Harness VLA. The rules are code. No model calls. Extendable Easy to evolve new tasks. Data engine COAP evolves fast, runs fast and works across episodes, so it generates trajectories efficiently for VLA. article.body:
COAP reaches 70.24% on simulated RoboDojo tasks

The paper’s Code-Only-as-Policy (COAP) approach was evaluated on 42 bimanual tasks in RoboDojo. It does not identify a physical robot or report its joint count, gripper configuration or payload capacity. COAP code tracks robot, environment and task state from camera images and proprioception, then makes decisions without a VLM or VLA at test time.

Coding agents developed the shared code library offline using development episodes in simulation; the benchmark’s test episodes were not used for development. The reported 70.24% success rate is a simulation result, not evidence of physical deployment. The authors identify accurate state representation and robust code logic as limits; no real-world trial is reported.
